html:
Dashdorjiin Natsagdorj (1906 to 1937) was a Mongolian poet, playwright and writer, the founder of modern Mongolian literature. His poem My Native Land (1933), a hymn to Mongolia's mountains, rivers and herds, is learned by heart by Mongolian schoolchildren.

Born into a family of minor nobles near Urga, he joined the new government as a young man after the revolution of 1921 led by Sükhbaatar, working as a secretary and in the party's youth league. In 1926 he went to study in Leningrad and then in Germany. He wrote short stories in a new, plain style, and Three Fateful Hills (1934), a drama of love and power before the revolution, which became Mongolia's best known opera.

He was arrested in 1932, released, and lived under suspicion as the purges began. He died in 1937, aged 30, in unclear circumstances, as the great terror was starting that also destroyed Mongolia's monasteries. He is honoured today as a national poet of Mongolia.
